items.question: Should we force landlords to install insulation before renting their property to a new tenant?

It is the landlords responsibility to ensure this is done. In order to become a landlord the government should place requirements on landlords. If the insulation is top notch, tenants won't have to spend much on heating their homes. This will reduce energy usage throughout the country. items.question: Should we increase the tax rate on people who earn above a certain amount?
items.statement: In conclusion, we should increase the tax rate on people who earn above a certain amount. The current system of taxation is outdated and does not take into account the cost of living and the inequality of wealth in the UK. By increasing the tax rate on the higher earners, it would allow increased funding for social welfare and services across the UK, such as the NHS. It would make society fairer, allow wealth to distribute among classes and would also allow people to contribute to the economy in a way that is proportional to their income.

items.question: Should the government introduce a higher minimum wage for workers under 18?
items.statement: In general, the group was in favour of a higher minimum wage for workers under 18. However, the group was not in favour of an increase in the minimum wage in the short term, due to the potential inflationary impact of such a move. The group was in favour of a gradual increase in the minimum wage over the next few years, as this would allow for businesses to adjust to the change in the minimum wage. The group was also in favour of the introduction of a living wage, which would be set at a level that would allow for a worker to live comfortably. The group was also in favour of the introduction of a higher minimum wage for workers under 18, as they often do the same level of work that older workers do, whilst getting paid less for it. They often face significant financial difficulties, and being able to remunerate them for their labour to a greater extent would allow for these difficulties to be alleviated. Furthermore, wages have not risen with inflation for decades, reducing prospects for younger people to have savings and financial security. A higher minimum wage would go some way in addressing these issues.

items.question: Has the Internet been a net positive for humanity?
items.statement: The Internet has been a net positive for humanity.  It has provided easy access to data that would otherwise be difficult to obtain for the average individual.  It has become a fabric of our lives in lots of ways.  Whether that be investigating what a medical problem may or may not be, to investigating work related issues or keeping in contact with friends and loved ones across the world.  The term, "I'll google that" is as familiar as any reference to looking things up.  It is interwoven into our very existence.  It does however also enable nefarious activities but as with any advancement, be that faster engines for cars, or fast food, there are always areas that can be exploited.  Everything is completely at your fingertips today and is enabled by the internet.  Whether that be sending cash, ordering food, paying bills, keeping tabs on your children via car driving apps, the list is endless.  Whilst the opportunity for harm to result from use of the internet, we believe the good outweighs the bad and we need legislation to frame the use of the internet to prevent misuse.

items.quote_b: One problem is the amount of misinformation, malicious information, trolling and harmful content that is out there - it has certainly provided a platform for nasty and dishonest people to cause lots of harm.

items.statement: Children should be allowed to walk home from school on their own, but only after certain requirements are met. items.question: Is it possible to create a sustainable food supply?
items.statement:
It is possible to create a sustainable food supply, but only on a small scale and not on a global scale.
The group agreed that in order to create a sustainable food supply on a global scale, there would have to be a global effort. The world is too large and diverse for this to be possible. There are too many different cultures, belief systems, and different levels of wealth. There are too many different types of climates and environments to make this possible. The participants agreed that this is an idealistic idea that is not practical. However, they did agree that it is possible to create a sustainable food supply on a small scale, such as a small community or a small group of people. In this case, the people would have to work together, cooperate, and be willing to make sacrifices in order to make it work. This would require a strong leader to bring everyone together and to keep everyone on the same page. The participants also agreed that it would be a very difficult thing to accomplish, but it would be possible.
